findings.title: Taking the greater XP total loses independently earned XP
findings.problem: The legacy-write merge retains both devices' answer occurrences but sets XP to greatest(stored XP, incoming XP). These are cumulative snapshots, not independent earned amounts, so their maximum does not represent the merged history.
findings.failure_scenario: Both tabs start at 100 XP. The new client earns 10 XP and saves 110. An already-open old client independently earns 20 XP and saves 120 without a revision. The trigger preserves both new answers but stores 120 XP instead of 130. Reloading makes that loss permanent. The same maximum-based approach also mishandles legitimate decreases such as flashcard Undo.
findings.fix: Merge earned changes relative to a shared baseline or identifiable operations, rather than taking the maximum of cumulative totals. If old clients cannot provide enough information for a safe merge, require a controlled refresh instead of silently accepting an incorrect total. Add a SQL regression with independent gains from a nonzero shared baseline and an Undo regression.

findings.title: Date-only review stamps cannot order same-day flashcard grades
findings.problem: nextSchedule writes only a calendar-date seen value, while the new mergeScheduleMap in guest.js promises to retain the later review. For two reviews on the same day, their stamps tie and the local snapshot wins regardless of when either review occurred. The SQL compatibility merger instead always retains the stored entry on that tie, dropping subsequent same-day changes.
findings.failure_scenario: Two current clients load the same card schedule. Tab A grades Good at 09:00, producing a seven-day interval. Tab B grades Again at 10:00 and saves first, making the card due today. A's delayed save conflicts and merges afterward. Both entries have the same seen date, so A's older seven-day schedule overwrites the newer Again grade. The student no longer sees a card they just failed to recall.
findings.fix: Record a review-operation timestamp or ordered operation identifier alongside the LOCAL due date, preserve it through saves, and use it consistently in both mergers. Handle legacy date-only ties explicitly, including same-day regrades and Undo. Test a newer Again grade followed by an older Good snapshot arriving late.

findings.title: Legacy answer replay collapses distinct repeated occurrences
findings.problem: replayUnseen tracks undated, attempt-less rows in a Set of legacySignature values. Two separate legacy answers with the same id, outcome, and metadata therefore become one ability update. reconcileProgress retains both rows in the merged log, but when a new canonical attempt is also present it replaces ability with this undercounted replay.
findings.failure_scenario: A new tab has an empty baseline. An older tab answers the same missed Pharmacology question incorrectly in two separate sittings, saving two identical legacy log rows and Pharmacology n=2. The new tab answers a different question and encounters a revision conflict. Reconciliation preserves all three log rows, but replayUnseen scores only the first legacy occurrence, leaving Pharmacology n=1 and the wrong theta. Readiness and adaptive selection subsequently use that corrupted ability.
findings.fix: Match legacy occurrences against the baseline with multiplicity, consuming each baseline occurrence once rather than deduplicating signatures globally. Replay every genuinely additional occurrence. Add a reconcileProgress regression containing two identical legacy rows plus a distinct live attempt, asserting both category counts and theta.

assessment: Not safe to release. Three persistence defects can discard earned XP, lose ability updates, or restore the wrong flashcard schedule. Findings are based on the supplied code; tests were not executed.
